questions.qtext: What is the function of the hidden layers in a multilayer perceptron (MLP)?

options.text: Hidden layers perform feature extraction and transformation
Hidden layers provide direct access to the input data
Hidden layers perform the final classification or regression task
Hidden layers are not necessary in an MLP

questions.solution:
(a)
The hidden layers in a multilayer perceptron (MLP) perform feature extraction and transformation by applying nonlinear transformations to the input data. Each hidden layer learns increasingly abstract and complex representations of the input data, allowing the network to capture intricate patterns and relationships in the data.

questions.qtext: Which of the following represents the linkage criteria of hierarchical clustering?

options.text: The distance metric used for measuring dissimilarity between clusters.
The method used to initialize cluster centroids.
The number of iterations required for convergence.
The threshold used for merging clusters.

questions.solution:
(a, d)
(a) Describe the distance metric, which measure dissimilarity between clusters using method like Euclidean or Manhattan distance, tailored to the specific data.
(d) Outlines the threshold for merging clusters. This threshold sets the maximum dissimilarity permitted between cluster; if it’s exceed, cluster won’t merge.
Both are vital in hierarchical clustering, shaping cluster formation and merger based on data or cluster distances.

questions.qtext: How does a feedforward neural network differ from other types of neural networks?

options.text: Feedforward neural networks allow feedback connections between neurons.
Feedforward neural networks can only have one layer of neurons.
Feedforward neural networks do not contain any hidden layers.
In feedforward neural networks, information flows in one direction, from input to output, without cycles or loops.

questions.solution:
(d)
A feedforward neural network is a type of neural network where information flows in one direction, from the input layer through the hidden layers (if present) to the output layer, without any feedback connections or cycles. This means that the output of one layer serves as the input to the next layer, and there are no loops or recurrent connections that would allow information to flow back to previous layers.
